The Ski Pustertal Express train links the area.

about.text: A family-friendly, uncrowded mountain near Chewelah, north of Spokane, known for its glade skiing, long consistent slopes and light, dry powder. Nordic trails too.

A big, well-groomed resort in Hachimantai, Iwate, beside Towada-Hachimantai National Park, with 21 long trails on Mt. Maemori and Mt. Nishimori (Japan's longest average run, at 2.1 km), 828 m of vertical, gondolas, night skiing most nights and a season from December into early May. IHG hotels, including an InterContinental, sit at the base.

A big Twin Cities hill along the St. Croix River with 50 trails over 350 feet of vertical, the Landing Zone terrain park and night skiing. Founded on a family farm in 1962 and now owned by Vail Resorts.

about.text: Two linked plateau areas, Folgaria and Lavarone, with about 104 km of slopes up to 1,850 m on one pass, cult runs like the black Agonistica, two snow parks, boardercross, baby parks and sledding, plus snowshoeing and Cimbrian food and cheese.

about.text: A ski area between Trentino and Veneto linking Moena, Soraga, Falcade and the San Pellegrino Pass (about 2,000 m), with the Col Margherita panorama, the Tre Valli ski tour through three valleys, black runs including the Piavac and La Volata, and dawn skiing.

One of the world's largest resorts, with 249 km of pistes and 84 lifts from 1,250 m up to Pic Blanc at 3,330 m, and off-piste from Pic Blanc and the Dôme des Petites Rousses. Mostly south-facing, so it gets the sun, backed by heavy snowmaking. Its black runs include the Tunnel and the Sarenne.
A small Epic hill in the heart of Ohio's snowbelt east of Cleveland, with beginner to advanced slopes, moguls, terrain parks and Dew After Dark night skiing.

about.text: Skiers only, and proud of it: snowboards aren't allowed at this Little Cottonwood Canyon legend, which gets about 540 inches of snow a year. Long fall-line pitches and chutes, a strong local and family following, and old-school lodges at the base.

about.text: A Ladin-speaking valley around Corvara on the Sella Ronda circuit, with about 130 km of mostly easy and intermediate runs from about 1,320 to 2,550 m, 51 lifts and snowmaking on most slopes. Home of the Gran Risa, one of the toughest World Cup giant slalom courses.
Alaska's big resort in Girdwood, south of Anchorage, with about 650 inches of snow up top, a lot of steep terrain, an aerial tram and a 300-room hotel at the base. Night skiing Thursday to Saturday.

The highest ski area in Iwate, on the slopes of Mt. Iwate above Morioka, with about 600 m of vertical on seven runs that range from a steep 37-degree pitch to the gentle Twin Forest course through frost-covered firs. A hot spring is a short walk from the hotel, and the ski school offers backcountry tours.

Andermatt's Gemsstock is a steep, high freeride mountain above a former garrison village, and the SkiArena links it over the Oberalp Pass to Sedrun and Disentis, with the Glacier Express train tying the valleys together. The village averages about 6 m of snow a year at 1,435 m. Vail Resorts owns the lift company, and Andermatt has been rebuilt as a year-round resort with new hotels and a concert hall.

about.text: A family-owned hill west of Alexandria, about two hours from Minneapolis, with full snowmaking, 16 runs and 14 cross-country trails. Often one of the first Midwest areas to open and last to close, with night skiing on the alpine side.

About 25 miles east of Taos, with 560 skiable acres, roughly 2,000 ft of vertical, 80 trails and 210 inches of snow a season, plus snowmaking on 230 acres. More than half the terrain is intermediate, with three terrain parks and a 3.2-mile longest run. Open since 1966; most of its skiers come from Texas.
A revived, community-backed ski area in Wyoming's Bighorn National Forest, about 75 minutes from Sheridan: 500 acres and 40 trails with a good share of advanced terrain. Authentic and uncrowded.

Off the beaten path at the foot of Mt. Iwaki near Hirosaki, with heavy snow (around 320 inches a year by Indy's numbers), family-friendly groomers and what the resort calls Japan's largest halfpipe. Strong skiers come for steep tree runs and lift-accessed backcountry.

A steep, friendly mountain above Penticton with 80 trails over 1,112 acres, more than half advanced, plus groomers, steep tree runs, parks and about 224 inches of light Okanagan powder. Cozy village, friendly locals.

about.text: Arabba is the steep corner of the Sella Ronda, with north-facing runs off Porta Vescovo, and the Marmolada next door is the highest peak in the Dolomites. A cable car to Punta Rocca (about 3,265 m) starts La Bellunese, a run that drops nearly 1,900 m to Malga Ciapela.

A huge-snow resort in Niigata's Myoko area (Ikon lists an average of over 800 inches) where nearly 80% of the 520 acres is off-piste powder, with groomers for the rest and a hike to the Big Bowl summit for 360-degree views. Reachable by direct train from Tokyo and a free shuttle from Joetsu-Myoko station.

Colorado's high, rugged local favorite with a 13,050-foot summit, the steep moguls of Pallavicini and the East Wall, and a season that often runs into summer. Spring tailgating at the base is a tradition.
Anchorage's backcountry-skiing-with-lifts hill: groomed runs on the front side and big ungroomed terrain beyond.

On the San Francisco Peaks 15 miles north of Flagstaff, with Arizona's biggest vertical (2,300 ft, from 9,200 to 11,500 ft) and about 260 inches of snow a year. 777 acres and 55 trails, including hike-to terrain. Skiing here began in 1938; snowmaking with reclaimed water stays controversial because the peaks are sacred to 13 tribes.

The largest linked ski area in Graubünden: 225 km of pistes from 1,230 to 2,865 m, joined since 2013 by the Urdenbahn cable car between Arosa and Lenzerheide. Half the kilometres are easy, there are 43 lifts, and the Parpaner Rothorn at the top has a panoramic restaurant.

about.text: Four mountains on one ticket: Aspen Mountain above town, steep Aspen Highlands, family-friendly Buttermilk with its famous park, and Snowmass, bigger than the other three combined. The town of Aspen is one of skiing's great après and dining scenes.

Two peaks near North Conway: Attitash proper has narrow, classic New England trails with steep fall lines, while Bear Peak is wider, with more glades and long cruisers. A Learning Center and a big kids' area make it work for mixed groups, and North Conway's restaurants and outlets are minutes away.
A hidden gem near Oliver on the South Okanagan and West Kootenay border, with glades, about 275 inches of snow and minimal lift lines.

about.text: High on the Continental Divide above Banff, reached by an eight-person gondola, with up to nine metres of snow a year, the avalanche-gear-required Delirium Dive and the slopeside Sunshine Mountain Lodge.

Spain's largest and most visited ski resort, in the Val d'Aran on the north side of the Catalan Pyrenees, where an Atlantic climate brings a good snow record. About 160 km of marked pistes across the Baqueira, Beret and Bonaigua sectors, from 1,500 to 2,610 m, and long a favourite of the Spanish royal family.

about.text: Vail's polished neighbor, with three villages (Beaver Creek, Bachelor Gulch and Arrowhead), the Birds of Prey World Cup downhill and a dedicated beginner area at McCoy Park. Known for service touches and a calmer, upscale feel.
Utah's best-kept secret in far northern Utah near Garden City, with about 400 inches of snow a year, 828 acres and 1,700 feet of vertical. Family-focused, with parks and night skiing.

In the foothills of the Changbai Mountains in Jilin, with one of the largest verticals in Asia (about 870 m), 74 trails and a sheltered setting known for dry powder, calm weather and rime-ice forests. Billed as China's largest night-skiing area, with hot springs for afterwards. New to Ikon for 26/27.

A state-owned Catskills mountain in Highmount, run by ORDA since 2012, with 1,404 ft of vertical, 62 trails and snowmaking on about 96% of the terrain. The Catskill Thunder gondola opened in 2017; beginners have the lower mountain and the Thunderhawk Learning Area, and the longest run is about 2.3 miles.

about.text: Nonprofit trails right in Bethel village, run by Inland Woods + Trails: 24 km on 33 trails, more than half rated beginner, with backcountry terrain beyond the groomed loops. An easy add-on to a Sunday River trip.

Two mountains above Big Bear Lake on one ticket, Bear Mountain and Snow Summit, about two hours from Los Angeles. Bear Mountain is the park-focused side; Snow Summit has more classic cruising and cross-country trails.
Jack Frost's Poconos sister area, long known for terrain parks and as a learning hill, owned by Vail Resorts. Short runs, easy access from the Northeast metros.

The old Big Squaw, run since 2012 as a volunteer nonprofit to keep skiing affordable in the Moosehead Lake region. A triple chair climbs to a 2,950-foot summit with views over the lake and toward Katahdin, and there's a two-mile groomed run down, cat skiing on natural snow and Nordic loops.
A classic Upper Peninsula resort in Big Snow Country near Bessemer, with about 200 inches a year, 45 trails and a Bavarian-style base village with two restaurants. Mom-and-pop feel, real snow.

about.text: One of the biggest ski areas in North America: about 5,850 acres and 4,350 feet of vertical, with the Lone Peak Tram reaching an 11,166-foot summit. Mostly intermediate and advanced terrain, with lodging at the base.
A big, locally owned Okanagan resort with 119 runs over 2,765 acres, dry snow, night skiing and a ski-through village. Family-operated and world-class.

A small Arctic ski area in Swedish Lapland beside the Lapporten valley, with what it calls Sweden's third-biggest vertical, well-groomed slopes, off-piste plains beyond the lifts and quiet cross-country trails. On clear nights you can see the northern lights.

Mostly mellow, sunny cruising with some black diamonds, old-school lifts and a renovated mid-mountain cabin for European-style après. It nearly closed in 2023; Indy Pass's own Erik Mogensen bought it in 2026.

about.text: A community-minded ski area in Rumford with about 1,400 feet of vertical, Nordic trails and the Chisholm Ski Club behind it. Cheap passes, free skiing for young kids, tubing and free ski nights on some Wednesdays make it a family favorite.

Pennsylvania's highest skiable mountain, with a 3,142-foot summit and over 1,000 feet of vertical. The top-down layout has a 2-mile cruiser, bumpy steeps and what the resort calls the Mid-Atlantic's only bowl. Night skiing and parks too, about 30 minutes from Altoona and Johnstown.

Ontario's busiest resort on the Niagara Escarpment by Georgian Bay, with 720 feet of vertical, four terrain parks and a lively pedestrian village of hotels, shops and restaurants. A classic weekend from Toronto.
The biggest vertical in Pennsylvania, about 1,080 feet, with 40 trails, five terrain parks and night skiing and tubing. A dedicated beginner area and teaching hill, near the Lehigh Valley.

A non-profit area 16 miles above Boise, with 2,600 acres, about 1,800 ft of vertical and four high-speed quads. Five chairlifts run night skiing on 165 acres until 10 pm every night, and there are 23 miles of cross-country trails. Snowfall has run below its 200-250 inch average since 2011.

about.text: Vermont's highest base area, close to Burlington and locally owned, with the state's biggest night-skiing operation (a dozen trails under lights). Add about 100 km of Nordic and backcountry trails and the Blauvelt's Banks banked slalom, and it feels like a skier's mountain rather than a resort.
Two small areas next to Cuyahoga Valley National Park between Cleveland and Akron, with Dew After Dark night skiing and Polar Blast snow tubing. Owned by Vail Resorts.
A small family hill in North Dakota's Turtle Mountains, with nine trails, a terrain park, night skiing and an adaptive program for guests with disabilities.

about.text: The oldest ski area in the Berkshires, opened in 1932 in Pittsfield, and a night-skiing pioneer with floodlights since 1936. About 750 feet of vertical; new owners have been upgrading it since 2020. A handy, low-key in-town hill and a Learn to Turn partner.
An upscale northern Michigan resort near Boyne Falls with 60 runs, four terrain parks and night skiing. The Mountain Grand Lodge and Spa, with its indoor waterpark, makes it a family weekend base.
Five peaks above a historic, lively mining town, with lifts reaching nearly 13,000 feet. Gentle slopes on lower Peaks 8 and 9 for beginners and high bowls up top. Busy, social and easy to love.

Across Route 302 from the Mount Washington Hotel, which owns it, in the White Mountains: about 464 acres, 1,500 ft of vertical and about 100 trails. It averages over 200 inches of snow, makes snow on 92% of its trails and runs New Hampshire's only 8-person gondola. SKI readers once ranked it first in the East for snow, grooming and service.

Utah's southernmost resort, about 3.5 hours from Las Vegas, with a base at 9,600 ft and two peaks, Navajo and Brian Head, linked by a bridge over the highway. Navajo is mostly beginner and intermediate terrain; Brian Head Peak has the steeper runs. 660 acres and eight chairlifts.

A locally owned non-profit ski area in the Bridger Range, 16 miles north of Bozeman, with 2,000 acres, 2,600 ft of vertical and about 350 inches of snow. The Ridge is mostly hike-to expert terrain that needs a beacon and shovel. Since 1988 a blue light on Bozeman's Baxter Hotel has signaled two inches of new snow.
Utah's first ski resort, up Big Cottonwood Canyon, with deep Wasatch snow, five terrain parks, night skiing and a laid-back, snowboard-friendly history.

The Sun Mountain, seven miles from Manchester, Vermont, named for its southern exposure. 178 acres, 1,334 ft of vertical and 47 trails with six glades and three terrain parks; SKI ranked it among the top three kid-friendly mountains in the East. Fred Pabst Jr. cut the first trail in 1936, and the Long and Appalachian Trails cross the mountain.

about.text: An Eastern Townships mountain about an hour from Montreal, with several faces, snowparks and a big after-dark program; its lit terrain is among the largest in North America.
A small Clark County hill in Merrillan with a surprisingly advanced trail mix, parks, tubing and night skiing, plus a chalet restaurant with fireside patios.
McCall's mountain in the Payette National Forest, with about 320 inches of snow, nearly 2,000 acres and a charming, family-friendly feel. Indy holders get a discount on its cat skiing.
A small family resort in Virginia's Shenandoah Valley with eight trails, night skiing and tubing. Weekend après happens at Carter's Hütte.

about.text: A Burnsville hill on the south side of the Twin Cities, famous as the home hill and race club of Lindsey Vonn. Short runs, night skiing and a strong racing program.

A family-focused ski club in Colden, south of Buffalo, with 38 trails on 175 acres, a balanced trail mix, strong kids' programs and night skiing. No terrain parks; this is about family laps and lake-effect snow.

A standalone peak in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom with about 2,000 feet of vertical and a reputation for short lift lines, far from the southern-Vermont crowds. Home of Burke Mountain Academy, the ski-racing school, and three terrain parks from beginner to advanced. New owners bought it in 2025 and plan upgrades.

about.text: One of Michigan's oldest ski areas, near Cadillac, with three peaks (East, North and South) and the 42-room Mackenzie Lodge right at the base for ski-in/ski-out stays. Relaxed and homegrown.

About an hour from Ottawa, with Ontario's biggest public vertical (781 feet), bumps, steeper pitches and terrain parks, plus the longest beginner run and strong learn-to-ski programs. No night skiing; skating and snowshoe trails on site.

Town-owned and billed as the only East Coast ski area with ocean views, over Penobscot Bay. About 1,000 feet of vertical with glades and two terrain parks, plus the country's last original wooden toboggan chute, home of the National Toboggan Championships.

A big Poconos family resort with 800 feet of vertical, 35 trails and night skiing on every trail. A 453-room hotel with the Aquatopia indoor waterpark sits on the mountain, and nearly 40% of trails are beginner.
An unpretentious community hill just outside Rhinelander with 15 trails, a beginner-friendly mix and night skiing. New to Indy for 2026-27.
Ottawa's historic local hill in Chelsea, minutes from downtown, with 27 trails that lean intermediate and advanced, night skiing and parks. Generations of Ottawa families learned here.
A state-park resort in a high West Virginia valley with 47 trails, a surprising share of advanced terrain and about 117 inches of snow a year. Tubing, skating and cross-country skiing round it out.

A two-lift community hill near Asahikawa in central Hokkaido with eight runs, night skiing, cross-country trails and a kids' sledding area. The Rabbit course is for first-timers, and the snow is light Hokkaido powder (about 180 inches a year).

State-owned and proudly old-school in Franconia Notch, with the first passenger aerial tram in North America and a mostly challenging trail mix. Kinsman Glade and the Mittersill sidecountry draw experts, while Tuckerbrook and Brookside give beginners their own space. It faces north into the wind, so dress for the weather.

Steep, independent and community-owned in the southern Canadian Rockies, 2.5 hours from Calgary: 2,845 feet of vertical and mostly advanced chutes, bowls and fall-line runs, with few crowds.
North Carolina's first ski area, opened in 1961 above Maggie Valley, with a base above 4,600 feet, 18 trails, parks and night skiing. Family-focused and beginner-heavy.

Family-owned and straddling the Massachusetts-New York line, with 1,000 feet of vertical, steep runs like Ripper and Lynx, glades and three terrain parks. Night skiing runs Wednesday to Saturday, and there's a dedicated learning area and a big youth race program.

A small club in Cazenovia, open since 1941, with 500 feet of vertical, two lifts and a surprising mix of steeps, glades, groomers and gentle beginner trails. No night skiing or parks; a friendly, old-school day out.

A magnet for steep skiing and alpinists, with a lively town.

about.text: A semi-private club in the Finger Lakes with 875 feet of vertical and more advanced terrain than most hills its size, plus parks and night skiing. Non-members ski weekdays only; weekends are for members. Lessons are run by a strongly certified ski school.

The Catskills' big, steep mountain, about two and a half hours from Manhattan, with 1,600 feet of vertical and top-tier snowmaking. Expect classic New York steeps and busy weekends, plus a large learning center for first-timers.

A tiny ski area inside Olympic National Park near Port Angeles, with three lifts, about 400 inches of snow and views where mountains meet the sea. It runs on limited days and depends on the park road, so check before you go.
A small but busy Bloomington hill with 13 trails, nine lifts, innovative terrain parks and night skiing every day. A Twin Cities after-work and lesson favorite.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: Sweden's newest ski area, opened in 2019 near Idre in northern Dalarna, with 24 runs including the 3.2 km Långstigen, a funpark, a kids' area and club, a beginner conveyor, and a new six-seat express chair and seven new runs being built for 26/27.

about.text: Indy's days here work across the 12 ski areas of Innsbruck's SKI plus CITY pass, from the Nordkette, which rises straight out of the city, to Axamer Lizum, Patscherkofel, Kühtai and the Stubai Glacier: about 265 km of pistes up to around 3,000 m, open roughly October to May. The 2 days are issued as back-to-back days.

A Paznaun village linked over the Swiss border to duty-free Samnaun, with about 238 km of pistes and 45-plus lifts up from Idalp's wide easy runs and park to the steep Höllboden bowl. Ischgl is famous for its big après and party scene.
A Poconos mountain near the Lehigh River with longer runs than its sister area Big Boulder, owned by Vail Resorts. A straightforward regional day trip.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: Steep and legendary, with over 4,100 feet of continuous vertical from the tram and Corbet's Couloir for the bold. Teton Village at the base and the town of Jackson nearby keep the evenings lively.

about.text: Vermont's snow magnet near the Canadian border, with the most average snowfall in eastern North America by the resort's count (about 359 inches). It's known for roughly two dozen glades and the Face Chutes off the tram, some of the steepest marked lines in the East. The base has a hotel, ski-in/ski-out condos and the Pump House indoor waterpark, which makes it an easy family pick on a stormy day.

about.text: The Hakuba Valley's southernmost resort: a small, gentle hill (about 260 m of vertical, 70% beginner) with a lift designed for small children and some tree runs near the top.

access.notes: Bonus mountain. Ikon lists blackout dates for some bonus mountains without naming them, so they are shown here.

about.text: Southern New England's biggest resort, family-owned in Hancock, with about 1,150 feet of vertical, night skiing and slopeside lodging at the Country Inn. It was the first ski area to put up its own wind turbine. Strong on families and groomed cruising.

access.notes: Buy one day, get the next day free (one person, consecutive days). Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: Mammoth's quiet sibling near June Lake, with 1,500 acres of tree runs and off-piste powder and small crowds. A local favorite.

A budget-friendly Hokkaido mountain near Asahikawa, easy to reach from Asahikawa or Furano, with 25 runs, plenty of powder and lift-accessed tree and off-piste skiing. It's uncrowded apart from the odd gondola queue, with two or three days of terrain.

Billed as the closest ski area to Tokyo, a free seven-minute shuttle from Echigo-Yuzawa shinkansen station, with 100% natural snow, an on-site hot spring and sauna, and weekend night skiing until 2 a.m.

access.notes: 5 consecutive days total across the 10 Hakuba Valley areas. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: A family park at the southern end of the valley with about 490 m of vertical, 12 courses, a 150 m snow-tubing park, a snow escalator for kids and a Pokémon snow-adventure area.

A quiet glacier ski area at the head of Tyrol's Kaunertal, reached by the Kaunertal Glacier Road from Feichten, with runs between about 2,150 and 3,100 m, a terrain park and, as Indy puts it, no long queues. The smaller Fendels family area is included.

about.text: A family hill in a canyon near Ririe, 30 minutes east of Idaho Falls, with 27 trails over 640 acres, parks and night skiing. A Learn to Turn partner.
Silverton's tiny town hill: one lift, five trails and a small jump and rails. Affordable, relaxed and low-crowd, in one of Colorado's most dramatic mountain towns.
Three mountains in Summit County with night skiing on 15 trails and the progressive A51 terrain park, plus long groomers and lodging at the base. Close to Denver and popular with families.

access.notes: 7 days total across Fernie Alpine Resort, Kicking Horse, Kimberley Alpine Resort, Nakiska, Mont-Sainte-Anne and Stoneham (Resorts of the Canadian Rockies).

about.text: Steep and serious near Golden: 1,315 metres of vertical, about 75 inbounds chutes and the Golden Eagle Express gondola to the top. A favorite for strong skiers.

The Beast of the East: the biggest ski area in the eastern US, with six peaks, about 3,000 feet of vertical and one of the longest seasons around. There's terrain for everyone, from Snowshed's learning slopes to Outer Limits' moguls and the Canyon's double blacks, and the Access Road bars make it the region's liveliest après scene. Pico, a few miles away, is a quieter, old-school mountain on the same ticket.

access.notes: 7 days total across Fernie Alpine Resort, Kicking Horse, Kimberley Alpine Resort, Nakiska, Mont-Sainte-Anne and Stoneham (Resorts of the Canadian Rockies).

about.text: A sunny East Kootenay mountain above the town of Kimberley, with 80 runs, a solid advanced share, terrain parks and night skiing.

about.text: A sunny Nordic club inside Kimberley's city limits, with 30 km of groomed double track, single track and a 3.3 km loop lit every night. Top-tier grooming.

A family ski area in East Madison run by the Hoyt family, with slopeside lodging, lessons for every age and kids' programs. There's also 20 km of cross-country and snowshoe trails, a tubing hill and an ice rink, which makes it a relaxed pick for families with mixed interests.

access.notes: Holiday blockouts apply.

about.text: Remote, snowy and steep, south of Lake Tahoe in the Eldorado National Forest: roughly 350 to 500 inches a year and The Wall's chutes, with most terrain advanced or expert.

A self-contained resort in the hills of Akaigawa, Hokkaido, with about 15 m (49 ft) of snow a year, 23 courses on about 1,200 acres, tree runs, backcountry and night skiing. Two hotels at the base have over 500 rooms between them, with hot springs and kids' areas.

Home of the Hahnenkamm races on the Streif, one of the hardest downhills in the world, and a medieval, mostly car-free town with a jet-set crowd. KitzSki covers about 168 km of slopes and 56 lifts on the Hahnenkamm, Kitzbüheler Horn and beyond, linked by a 3S gondola with a record-high span.

access.notes: 5 days total across Skicircus Saalbach Hinterglemm Leogang Fieberbrunn, Schmittenhöhe (Zell am See) and Kitzsteinhorn (Kaprun) (Saalbach, Zell am See and Kaprun). Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: Austria's first glacier ski area, above Kaprun, opened in 1965 and reaching 3,029 m at the top station (the summit is 3,203 m). Its altitude gives one of the longest seasons in the Alps, and it pairs with the Maiskogel home hill in Kaprun and Zell am See's Schmittenhöhe on one pass.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: Sweden's largest family-owned ski resort, in Sälen, voted the country's best for families, with about 26 km of piste on 41 runs, 22 lifts including a heated-seat gondola, 10 lit runs and three snowparks led by what's billed as Sweden's best park.

access.notes: 7 days total across the 12 Dolomiti Superski areas. Valid 15 Nov 2026 to 15 Apr 2027.
5 days total across the 12 Dolomiti Superski areas. Valid 15 Nov 2026 to 15 Apr 2027.

about.text: A dome-shaped Dolomites mountain in South Tyrol's Puster Valley with lifts converging on the 2,275 m summit from every side: 121 km of runs, 31 lifts, about 1,375 m of vertical, heavy snowmaking and five black runs, including the Erta.

A Slovenian ski area in the Kamnik Alps, about 8 km from Ljubljana-Brnik airport (which it calls the closest ski resort to an international airport in Europe), 25 km from the capital and 35 km from Bled, with 30 km of runs and a terrain park.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: Built for the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics speed races, where Tommy Moe won the downhill on the Bernhard Russi-designed Olympiabakken, and still a regular men's World Cup stop. About 850 m of vertical, heavy snowmaking, a terrain park, night skiing and 120 km of cross-country trails.

Eight or so villages, from Champagny and Montchavin up to Belle Plagne, on one huge area with 225 km of slopes between 1,250 and 3,250 m. Since 2003 the Vanoise Express cable car links it to Les Arcs as Paradiski. The 1992 Olympic bobsleigh track is here, and Les Coches is the family village.

Switzerland's freestyle capital, in Graubünden above Laax, Flims and Falera, with five snowparks, what LAAX calls the world's largest halfpipe and a new indoor Hall of Freestyle. The lifts climb to the Vorab, and the rocksresort sits right at the valley station.

access.notes: 7 days total across Banff Sunshine, Lake Louise and Mt Norquay (SkiBig3).
5 days total across Banff Sunshine, Lake Louise and Mt Norquay (SkiBig3).
2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: One of North America's biggest ski areas, with 145 runs and back bowls across four faces and gondola views of glaciers and peaks in Banff National Park. A World Cup stop with a big end-of-season party.

About 15 km from Jilin City, with 50 trails and seven lifts, rime-frosted trees, night skiing under lights and views of Songhua Lake from the top. Named China's best ski resort many years running. New to Ikon for 26/27.

A historic state-park ski area in the Laurel Highlands, opened in 1940 with trails laid out by Hannes Schneider. About 760 feet of vertical, half the trails easy, and a lodge full of Pennsylvania ski memorabilia.

Flaine's high bowl and the villages of Samoëns, Morillon, Les Carroz and Sixt share the Grand Massif's 267 km of pistes, up to 2,561 m. Flaine, with one of the best snow records in the Alps, is Marcel Breuer's brutalist purpose-built resort, and the Cascade run is 14 km long.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: The biggest vertical in eastern Canada, 770 metres, in Charlevoix about 90 minutes from Quebec City. You park at the top and ski toward the St. Lawrence River, with panoramic views the whole way down.

about.text: A busy little club in Washington's Bavarian village, with a small alpine hill, 26 km of Nordic trails and night skiing on the Nordic side.

France's second-oldest ski resort, with about 220 km of runs and 2,300 m of vertical, from the village at 1,650 m to 3,600 m. The Mont de Lans and Girose glaciers, Europe's largest skiable glacier, open for summer skiing from June to September, and the snowpark is one of the biggest in Europe. The Jandri 3S reaches the glacier in 17 minutes.

access.notes: 7 consecutive days. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: Courchevel, Méribel, Les Menuires, Val Thorens and their neighbours share one lift system that has been on a single pass since 1971, billed as the largest linked ski area in the world: about 180 lifts and roughly 500 to 600 km of pistes depending on who measures. It runs from 600 m at Brides-les-Bains to 3,230 m, and most of the terrain is easy or intermediate, with long cruisers like the 12 km Cîme de Caron run.

access.notes: New for 26/27.
New for 26/27.

about.text: A large area in the Belledonne range above Grenoble with two sides: busy Prapoutel and quieter Le Pleynet. Sheltered from Atlantic storms, it gets heavy snow that fills unpisted powder bowls, served by modern lifts. New to Indy for 26/27.

Four purpose-built villages above Bourg-Saint-Maurice, three of them modernist designs by Charlotte Perriand, with a funicular to the TGV station in about 7 minutes. From the Aiguille Rouge a 7 km piste drops 2,026 m to Villaroger. The Vanoise Express joins it to La Plagne as Paradiski, 425 km in all.

access.notes: New for 26/27.
New for 26/27.

about.text: A family resort about an hour from Geneva, with 120 km of slopes between 1,200 and 2,500 m spread across Savoie and Haute-Savoie and views from Mont Blanc to the Beaufortain. Known for reliable snow and runs that wind down through valleys and past chalets. New to Indy for 26/27.

access.notes: Indy's discounted third day isn't offered here.
Indy's discounted third day isn't offered here.

about.text: The Torrent ski area and the Gemmi plateau above Leukerbad, the biggest natural thermal spa resort in the Alps, with groomed runs, views of Switzerland's 4,000 m peaks and 18 km of cross-country trails including high routes on the Gemmi. Indy's discounted third day isn't offered here.

Finland's biggest and most popular ski resort, in Kittilä in Finnish Lapland, with 26 lifts, a long, snow-sure season, night skiing under lights through the polar night, over 230 km of cross-country trails, a World Cup slalom each November and a real après scene.
A night-skiing machine eight miles from Gettysburg: every trail lit seven nights a week, about 620 feet of vertical and a 116-room hotel at the slope. An easy trip from Baltimore and DC.
McCall's community hill with four groomed runs, a terrain park and Central Idaho's only night skiing, served by a single T-bar.

A high valley town at 1,816 m by the Swiss border, with 115 km of runs and 31 lifts on two sides of the valley, Carosello 3000 and Mottolino. Many goods are duty-free, and it hosted snowboarding and freestyle at the 2026 Winter Olympics. The season runs from late November to early May.
Thunder Bay's ski hill, with 18 trails, parks, night skiing and views over Lake Superior. Friendly staff and northern-wilderness charm.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: A small mountain village in southern Härjedalen with 25 slopes, from kids' runs to Rännan, Sweden's second-steepest groomed slope at 42 degrees, good off-piste, rare lift queues and 122 km of snow-sure cross-country tracks.

A busy, well-run White Mountains resort right off I-93 in Lincoln, spread across North Peak, South Peak and a summit gondola with mountain views. It's known for its terrain parks and long groomers, with lodging and restaurants in Lincoln and the slopeside Mountain Club. Black Ridge, 272 acres of expert glades in the national forest, is slated for winter 2027-28.
Montana's best-kept secret near Darby: about 350 inches of snow, 1,800 acres and 69 trails at a relaxed, old-school area.
A small family hill in Auburn with 233 feet of vertical, night skiing, terrain parks and racing programs. A good learning spot with a brewpub at the base that's open year-round.

about.text: Skiing like it used to be, between the Okanogan and Methow valleys near Twisp: 300 acres, 14 alpine trails, short waits, a small-town welcome and 10-plus km of groomed Nordic trails. A Learn to Turn partner.

A high, snowy local favorite 53 miles west of Denver, with terrain up to 13,010 feet, about 324 inches of snow, 1,800 acres and free snowcat rides along the Continental Divide. No frills, just skiing.
The Midwest's big mountain on Minnesota's North Shore: four peaks, a gondola to Moose Mountain and views over Lake Superior. Condos and townhomes nearby, with a family-friendly reputation.

A skier-owned co-op in Vermont's Mad River Valley, where the Single Chair has carried one skier at a time since 1948 and snowboarding is still banned by member vote. Narrow trails, little grooming and snowmaking on only 15% of the mountain keep it natural: 2,037 ft of vertical and 60 trails under the motto Ski It If You Can.
Billed as Ohio's largest ski and snowboard resort, near Zanesfield, with Dew After Dark night skiing and a tubing park with lanes over 1,000 feet long. Owned by Vail Resorts.

A tree skier's playground in northern Nagano, with 12 official tree runs, about 60% of courses left ungroomed and deep "Madapow" in midwinter (around 400 inches a year). About 30 minutes from Iiyama shinkansen station, and close to Myoko Suginohara, Arai and Shiga Kogen. New to Ikon for 26/27.

access.notes: 7 consecutive days total across the 6 Skirama Dolomiti areas. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: One of Italy's most fashionable ski towns, in the Brenta Dolomites, linked with Pinzolo, Folgarida and Marilleva into about 150 km of runs and 57 lifts. Its tree-lined pistes include the Canalone Miramonti, home of the 3Tre night slalom, and there's a large snow park and 40 km of Nordic trails.

A cult favorite in southern Vermont: about 1,500 feet of vertical, steep old-school pitches and the most tree skiing in that part of the state. It's small, independent and proud of it, with a loyal crowd, a terrain park, some night skiing and a newer learning area with a carpet lift. Best on natural-snow days.
A crowd-free hidden gem south of Kimberly, Idaho, with about 230 inches of snow and a steeper-than-average mix on 22 trails. No parks; family-friendly.

An easy run from Tokyo in Minamiuonuma, Niigata, with 26 courses for every level, a longest run of about 6 km, heavy snow and night skiing. The day lodge connects straight to the gondola and has hot springs and a panoramic bath overlooking the slopes, with two hotels on site.

A village ski area in the Krkonoše (Giant Mountains), the Czech Republic's highest range, with mostly intermediate and advanced runs, a terrain park, groomed cross-country tracks and views of Sněžka, the country's highest peak.

access.notes: Buy one day, get the next day free (one person, consecutive days). Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: California's big mountain: 3,500 acres, an 11,059-foot summit, eight Unbound terrain parks and a season that often runs from November into May or later. Après is a scene here: weekend parties at Canyon Lodge's sundeck have DJs spinning from a gondola car, and the pedestrian village keeps going after dark.

about.text: A family-owned cross-country ski resort near Callaway, Minnesota, where you stay, eat and ski in one place. Known for its home-style food and quirky, welcoming lodges.
Atlantic Canada's big mountain in Newfoundland's Humber Valley: 1,700 feet of vertical, 43 trails and nearly 200 inches of snow a year, with night skiing, parks and on-site lodging at Marble Villa.

about.text: Jasper National Park's mountain, with 91 runs on four faces, about 3,000 feet of vertical and views down to the town of Jasper. Quieter and more remote than the Banff resorts.

about.text: Five minutes from Marquette with Lake Superior views, about 210 inches of snow a year, 29 runs including nine glades, and night skiing. Mostly intermediate and advanced. A Learn to Turn partner.

about.text: A four-season Shenandoah Valley resort with 1,100 feet of vertical, a solid share of advanced runs, a dedicated learning area, parks and night skiing. Resort lodging sits next to the slopes.

about.text: Privately owned, powder-focused and Quebec's highest-altitude skiing, on Mont du Midi near Saint-Philémon. Two lifts serve 420 acres, mostly advanced, with glades and around 144 inches of snow a year. A Learn to Turn partner too.

access.notes: 5 days total across the 5 Zillertal areas. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: Mayrhofen sits between the Penken and the Ahorn in Tyrol's Zillertal: the Penken links to Finkenberg and Hippach and holds the Harakiri, billed as Austria's steepest groomed run, while the Ahorn is mostly easy and intermediate. The village is snowboard-minded, with a well-known terrain park and a lively après scene.

Manchester's in-town hill at Exit 8 off I-93: 11 trails, full snowmaking, terrain parks and a big beginner area with two carpets. The tubing hill and the bar's Saturday-night après make it an easy after-work or family stop.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: France's original purpose-built ski resort, created by the Rothschilds in the 1920s as a rival to St. Moritz and still one of the most affluent in the Alps. The Évasion Mont-Blanc area adds up to about 445 km of mostly easy and intermediate runs on Mont d'Arbois, Rochebrune and Côte 2000, plus 65 km of cross-country trails.

Middlebury College's own ski area on Worth Mountain: three lifts, about 1,000 feet of vertical and a 1938 log-cabin base lodge, the oldest standing in the country. Small, relaxed and mostly natural snow on the backside, with about 200 inches a year. A good quiet day rather than a destination.

about.text: A nonprofit Nordic center in Wisconsin's Northwoods with a big trail network on about 6,500 acres, a ski shop and school, and family events.

On the east side of the Cascades, 12 miles from Wenatchee, with about 200 inches of snow and over 300 sunny days a year. 2,000 acres and 2,250 ft of vertical, mostly intermediate. A B-24 bomber crashed in the basin in 1944, and a wing now sits above Bomber Bowl; Olympic champion Bill Johnson trained here.

Connecticut's best-known ski area, in Cornwall, where founder Walt Schoenknecht helped pioneer the snow gun. About 650 feet of vertical, 99% snowmaking and busy night skiing for the tri-state area, plus snow tubing.

Korea's largest ski resort, in Pyeongchang, Gangwon, which hosted the technical alpine races of the 2018 Winter Olympics and earlier World Cups. 31 slopes and a 3.7 km gondola up to about 1,458 m, with a season from November to early April, a big base lodge and an indoor water park.

On Monarch Pass at the Continental Divide, 20 miles west of Salida, skied since 1939. 54 trails, most of them advanced or expert, an extreme area called Mirkwood, two terrain parks and 1,635 acres of cat skiing in bowls, chutes and trees. An expansion into No Name Basin was approved in 2024.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: The linked Les Houches and Saint-Gervais area facing Mont Blanc, from about 1,000 to 1,900 m, with runs through fir forest, 360-degree views of the Mont Blanc range, the Verte des Houches World Cup piste, snowmaking and the Tramway du Mont-Blanc included on the pass. Helly Hansen's free day is for the Chamonix-valley (Les Houches) side.

A steep, snowy mountain by the Saguenay fjord in L'Anse-Saint-Jean: about 225 inches a year, glades and moguls, and what it calls the largest patrolled, marked backcountry sector east of the Rockies. It also claims the province's best après.
Called Quebec's ski kindergarten: a small hill west of Montreal in an old-growth forest, with 15 trails, a terrain park, night skiing and a big lesson program.
An Eastern Townships favorite famous for glades at every level, with 60 trails, about 140 inches of snow a year and a genuinely Québécois feel. Its après is among the region's best.
A human-scaled hill near Rouyn-Noranda that's mostly advanced, with parks, a dozen night sessions a season, tubing and an après bar in a warm lodge.

access.notes: 7 days total across Fernie Alpine Resort, Kicking Horse, Kimberley Alpine Resort, Nakiska, Mont-Sainte-Anne and Stoneham (Resorts of the Canadian Rockies).

about.text: A big mountain 40 km from Quebec City with over 2,000 feet of vertical on three sides and the most vertical for night skiing in Canada. Canada's largest Nordic center, over 200 km of trails, sits next door.

Scranton's mountain, about two hours from New York and Philadelphia, with 1,000 feet of vertical, full snowmaking and night skiing. It bills its steepest runs as Pennsylvania's steepest, and the wide-open trails usually have short lift lines. A summer waterpark shares the hill.
Missoula's mountain, about 30 minutes from downtown, with 2,600 feet of vertical, a lot of advanced terrain and powder, and a cozy lodge. There's terrain for first-timers too.

access.notes: 7 consecutive days total across the 6 Skirama Dolomiti areas. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: Trento's own mountain, about 17 km from the city, with about 19 km of mostly intermediate runs and 900 m of vertical up to Palon at about 2,090 m, freeride and powder above Vason, a snowpark, winter night skiing and cross-country trails in the Viote valley.

access.notes: 7 days total across the 5 Valle d'Aosta areas. Valid 1 Nov 2026 to 31 May 2027.

about.text: Three valleys at the foot of Monte Rosa (Ayas/Champoluc, Gressoney and Alagna) linked by lifts into about 180 km of runs up to 3,275 m. The Alagna side is world-famous for freeride and ski-mountaineering lines.

Fairbanks' big hill, with 1,300 feet of vertical over 750 acres, gentle cruisers and steep blacks, and buses that carry you back to the top in place of chairlifts. Alaska Range views and northern lights.
A Thunder Bay family favorite for over 60 years, with 12 trails across 200 acres, night skiing, parks and a fireplace chalet looking out over the hill.

about.text: A Minnesota River Valley hill a mile south of Mankato with 19 trails, two parks, full snowmaking, night skiing, tubing and a beginner area. Short lift waits are part of the appeal.

A small resort in Yubari, close to New Chitose Airport and Sapporo, with dry Hokkaido powder, good tree skiing and a sheltered, lower position that often keeps it open when nearby resorts close for wind.

The closest big Vermont mountain to the New York and Boston metros, built around a broad main face of intermediate cruisers. Carinthia is the park hub with around ten terrain parks, the North Face has the steeper runs and Sunbrook is a quieter, scenic side. Fast six-pack chairs help with weekend crowds, and the Grand Summit hotel sits at the base.

An easy drive from Boston, with about 1,500 feet of vertical, near-total snowmaking and a balanced mix of terrain. It's a dependable day trip with views over Lake Sunapee, and the spring Slush Cup pond skim is a local tradition.
The closest big skiing to Los Angeles, about 90 minutes from downtown: 50 trails across two mountains, plenty of terrain parks and night skiing Wednesday to Sunday in peak season.

about.text: A Victorian resort with 22 lifts and the state's highest uplift capacity, 85 trails on more than 300 hectares, four terrain parks, a steep-leaning mix, big snowmaking, weekend night skiing in July and August, and cross-country trails to Mt Stirling. Lodges and a village sit on the mountain.
Cordova's ski hill, with about 350 inches of snow, around 30 runs, a beginner rope tow and a historic 1939 single chair.

about.text: An NZSki field in the Southern Alps above the Canterbury Plains, 35 minutes from Methven and under two hours from Christchurch, usually the first Southern Hemisphere field to open each season. About 680 m of vertical, big off-piste, expert terrain at the Towers and South Face, and terrain parks. No lodging on the mountain; stay in Methven.
A Mississippi bluff hill close to La Crosse with 20 runs, river-valley views, night skiing and Damnation, a genuinely steep double black. The historic double A-frame chalet sets the mood.

access.notes: 7 days total across Banff Sunshine, Lake Louise and Mt Norquay (SkiBig3).

about.text: Banff's own mountain, minutes from town, skied since 1926: the North American chair serves some of the continent's toughest steeps, with night skiing and a laid-back community vibe.

about.text: A family-run mountain in Greenwood, near Bethel, that bills itself as Maine's most affordable. About 1,000 feet of vertical on 14 trails, daily lessons, youth camps and plenty of room to roam without crowds.
Oregon's largest ski area, 22 miles from Bend, with 4,300-plus acres and lift-served skiing 360 degrees off the summit on clear days.

At the end of the road past Glacier, about 75 minutes from Bellingham, with about 641 inches of snow a year and the world-record 1,140 inches of 1998-99. 1,000 acres and 1,589 ft of vertical, with steep in-bounds lines, backcountry access and no slopeside hotels. Home since 1985 of the Legendary Banked Slalom snowboard race.
A small Epic hill near Detroit with short runs and Dew After Dark night skiing. Good for after-work laps and learning.

Saranac Lake's town hill, minutes from downtown: one lift, seven trails and night skiing, where generations of local kids learned. A true hometown feel with Adirondack snow.

The closest Tahoe resort to Reno, with the region's highest base at 8,260 ft and about 350 inches of snow a year. 1,200 acres and 70-plus trails, half of them advanced or expert, including the Chutes: opened in 2004 and some of the steepest, most consistent terrain in Tahoe.

Tanigawa above Minakami in Gunma (formerly Tanigawadake Tenjindaira), with about 15 m of snow a year, steep terrain including the 3 km Tajirizawa course, and the Minakami hot-spring towns below. About an hour from Tokyo by shinkansen to Jomo-Kogen plus a 30-minute drive, the closest Ikon resort to the capital.
Five minutes from the highway in Minamiuonuma, Niigata, with very heavy snow (Indy's average is close to 400 inches), wide easy main slopes with mountain views, steeper sections and terrain parks.
Northern BC's best-kept secret near Fort St. James: a community-run nonprofit with steep runs, glades, a terrain park, excellent grooming and what it calls the longest T-bar in North America.

On Mt. Myoko in Niigata, with about 1,100 m of vertical and what's billed as Japan's longest run, an 8.5 km cruise from summit to base. Wide-open runs, 38-degree powder steeps on the Super Giant and Super Mogul trails, and the hot-spring village of Myoko Kogen below. Snowfall averages about 13 m a year.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: A mountain resort in Voss about two hours from Bergen airport, known for some of the heaviest snowfall in Europe, with 22 mostly wide, open slopes, two six-seat express chairs, a kids' area at the base by the hotel, terrain parks and nearby backcountry.

Hoshino Resorts' mountain above Lake Inawashiro in Fukushima, with a sunny south side of long, varied runs and a north side known for dry, light, frequently refreshed powder. The top of the Alts Express looks over Mt. Bandai and the lake, often above a sea of clouds.

access.notes: 7 days total across Fernie Alpine Resort, Kicking Horse, Kimberley Alpine Resort, Nakiska, Mont-Sainte-Anne and Stoneham (Resorts of the Canadian Rockies).

about.text: The 1988 Olympic alpine venue, 83 km west of Calgary in Kananaskis Country, with mostly intermediate cruising and reliable snowmaking. An easy day from the city.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: A mountain right behind the Arctic city of Narvik, rising from near sea level to over 1,000 m with views over the Ofotfjord to the Lofoten wall, lift-accessed freeride of up to about 1,100 m, floodlit skiing under the northern lights and spring skiing under the midnight sun. Narvik hosts the 2029 Alpine World Championships.

A local hill in Nayoro in northern Hokkaido, known for very cold, dry powder and the sun pillars that form in the frigid air, with runs for kids, seniors and backcountry skiers alike and night skiing.

about.text: Four resorts around Mt. Niseko Annupuri in Hokkaido (Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village and Annupuri) on one lift pass, in a town that averages over 9 m of snow a year. Backcountry is reached through patrol-controlled gates, Hanazono runs cat skiing, and Hirafu is Japan's most international ski village, with plenty of restaurants and bars.

about.text: Under two hours from Oslo above Lake Krøderen, with about 1,000 m of vertical and a mostly easy mix with three kids' areas, two terrain parks and night skiing. It hosted the alpine races of the 1952 Oslo Olympics.

access.notes: Holiday blockouts apply.

about.text: North Lake Tahoe's polished resort, known for long groomers, terrain parks and a village with a winter skating rink. A comfortable, family-friendly base near Truckee.

about.text: A Western Upper Peninsula hill near the Wisconsin line with 500 feet of vertical and 17 mostly intermediate trails. Scenic and cozy, and a Learn to Turn partner.

One of Japan's oldest ski resorts, rising straight out of a hot-spring village in Nagano with 13 free public bath houses. About 54 km of runs and 21 lifts fan out from the village, and the Dosojin fire festival lights up mid-January. Austrian pioneer Hannes Schneider taught here in the 1930s.

resorts.learnToTurn: Learn to Turn partner in 25/26: Indy's beginner pass (lift ticket for beginner terrain, a lesson and rentals, 3 days for $189). The 26/27 list isn't out yet.

about.text: A family-owned Harbor Springs favorite with 53 runs on three faces, parks and night skiing. It calls itself the place where skiers go, and it has a loyal following for its well-kept snow.
A tiny, community-funded beginner hill in Plymouth with one lift, two trails, a small park, tubing and night skiing. Perfect for a first day.

Skiing above Gatlinburg on the edge of the Great Smoky Mountains, reached by a two-mile aerial tram from downtown. Ten trails, parks and night skiing, plus skating, a mountain coaster and other year-round attractions.

Austria's highest parish, at 1,930 m, linked with Hochgurgl into one area among peaks over 3,500 m and several glaciers. Winters are cold and very snowy, with about 475 cm (187 in) a year and heavy snow from October to May.

A cross-border network of seven areas around Oberstdorf in Germany and the Kleinwalsertal in Austria, including the Nebelhorn, the linked Fellhorn and Kanzelwand, and the Ifen, so you can ski two countries in a day. About two hours from Munich by car or train.

A high pass village in the Salzburg Alps at about 1,630 m, which bills itself as Austria's snowiest resort, with around 100 km of groomed runs in a circuit around the village, lifts up to 2,313 m, night skiing and a lively village with plenty of après.

A southern Vermont favorite for families and cruisers: about 2,200 feet of vertical, near-total snowmaking and grooming that readers rank among the country's best. Carpet lifts and a conveyor-loading quad make learning easy, while the South Face holds the double blacks and glades. Lodging and dining spread across the Clock Tower base, Jackson Gore and Solitude.

A town-owned hill near Morioka with a sheltered east-facing bowl that feels like a private resort on weekdays, with almost no competition for powder. Two traditional onsen sit at the base, along with simple Japanese food and lodging.

about.text: In the Miyagi highlands near Naruko Onsen, inside Kurikoma Quasi-National Park, with wide-open slopes under a volcanic backdrop and a mostly intermediate and advanced mix. Popular with families and with skiers dodging bigger resorts' crowds. New to Indy for 26/27.

A sunny southern Alps resort at 1,850 m on the edge of the Écrins National Park, with skiing up to 2,725 m, a steep-leaning mix of 61 runs and a terrain park. It carries France's Famille Plus label for family services.

about.text: A Nordic center on the Tug Hill Plateau, which gets over 200 inches of lake-effect snow: 18 km of classic and skate trails through mature forest, more than half rated beginner. Trailside lodging, rentals, fire pits and a snack bar.
An Eastern Townships mountain in Mansonville with 1,770 feet of vertical, 50 trails and lake and mountain views from the top. Well-groomed slopes and a cozy resto-bar.

about.text: A modern Trentino area a short drive from Trento, with 50 km of runs from about 1,040 to 2,125 m above Andalo and Fai della Paganella, views of the Brenta Dolomites, a snowpark, beginner slopes and night skiing on Tuesdays and Fridays. The US men's team has trained on its black Olimpionica.

Between Karuizawa and the hot-spring town of Kusatsu in Gunma, with the longest gondola in the Kanto region rising to about 2,100 m, a mostly easy 22-run mix, a very large terrain park and sunrise skiing. The season runs early December to early April.
Host of the 1960 Winter Olympics: six peaks on the Palisades side, linked by a base-to-base gondola to Alpine Meadows. Famous for its steep, technical terrain and a lively Olympic Valley village.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: One of North America's biggest verticals at about 1,300 metres, with 129 trails over nearly 3,000 acres, a slopeside village and the Panorama Springs pools.
Southern Indiana's ski area near Paoli, a day trip for much of the region, with short runs, the Arctic Blast tubing park and Dew After Dark night skiing. Owned by Vail Resorts.

access.notes: Holiday blockouts apply.

about.text: The largest lift-served ski resort in the US since joining with Canyons, linked by the Quicksilver Gondola. Historic Main Street, with its bars and restaurants, is a short walk from the Town Lift.
A friendly neighbourhood ski area in Alberta's Crowsnest Pass with 27 short trails, nearly half advanced, plus parks and night skiing. Good for families.

about.text: Family owned since it opened in 1963, about 30 minutes from Concord. Half the trails are novice, with magic carpets and a new family quad, and it's a popular night-skiing spot. Ski magazine once called it the best slalom terrain in New Hampshire, and it runs a strong youth race program.
A classic, old-school hill in Lakewood with 14 short trails among the pines, half of them advanced, and night skiing. Small-town charm.
Where the locals go for vertical, near Inkom in southeast Idaho: 2,200 feet of vertical, 1,100 acres and a mostly advanced trail mix. New to Indy for 2026-27.

A resort in New York's snowy southwest corner near Clymer, with about 200 inches a year, 27 mostly intermediate trails, three progressive terrain parks and night skiing. Resort lodging and dining are on site.

access.notes: 7 consecutive days total across the 6 Skirama Dolomiti areas. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: A small, high ski area in the heart of Stelvio National Park in Val di Sole, with 15 runs and 7 lifts from 1,400 to 3,000 m, a Kinderland, a funslope, ski-touring and snowshoe routes, and the Pejo thermal baths below. Kids born in 2019 or later ski free with a paying family member.

access.notes: Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card. Valid in the 2027 southern winter (roughly June to October 2027) on a 26/27 pass.

about.text: The largest ski resort in the Southern Hemisphere: four linked areas (Perisher Valley, Smiggin Holes, Guthega and Blue Cow) in the Snowy Mountains' Kosciuszko National Park, with about 45 lifts on 1,245 hectares, mostly intermediate terrain and big snowmaking. The Skitube rack railway tunnels up from Bullocks Flat. Owned by Vail Resorts.
Southern Carinthia's local mountain on the Slovenian border, with about 1,300 m of vertical, well-groomed slopes, traditional huts, wide views, a kids' area for beginners and ski-touring routes.
A community family hill near Grand Forks with 22 runs, about 700 feet of vertical and night skiing. Open mid-December to March.

about.text: A sunny, mostly intermediate ski area above Aosta, reached from the city by an 18-minute gondola, with 14 lifts up to about 2,700 m and views across the Valle d'Aosta's big peaks. Easy to pair with Aosta's Roman and medieval sights.
Two miles from Iron Mountain, with 35 trails from bunny hill to black diamonds and night skiing. The town's famous Pine Mountain ski jump is next door.
A small, family-friendly hill near Asahikawa in Hokkaido that can feel almost private on powder days. The draw is off-piste and sidecountry terrain off three lifts, and there's night skiing.

Tyrol's highest ski area, at the head of the Pitztal above Mittelberg, where an underground funicular and then a cable car carry you to the Hinterer Brunnenkogel at 3,440 m, home of Café 3440, Austria's highest café. A long season on the glacier with big, high-altitude terrain.

Indy's 2 days are for the whole area: use them at any of the resorts.

A high Andes resort near Aconcagua, 160 km from Santiago, built around the Hotel Portillo at 2,880 m. Lifts run from 2,548 to 3,310 m over 35 runs, with about 8.3 m of snow a year. It hosted the 1966 World Championships, where Jean-Claude Killy won, and is a summer training base for national ski teams.

Above Ogden in the Wasatch, with 8,000 skiable acres, 4,200 of them lift-served, and about 360 inches of snow a year, with cat skiing and guided tours beyond the lifts. Reed Hastings bought it in 2023 and runs it semi-private, with some lifts for homeowners; day tickets are capped to keep crowds down.
A gentle, family-friendly hill in Middlefield, reopened in 2014 after years closed. No expert terrain, lots of beginner runs, night skiing on most of the mountain, a freestyle park and snow tubing.
A family-owned hidden gem in Kimball, west of the Twin Cities, with mostly beginner and intermediate runs, three terrain parks, night skiing and a full-service restaurant.

about.text: On the northern edge of the Grand Mesa above Mesa, Colorado, with over 1,600 acres, mostly beginner and intermediate runs and big views. Family-friendly.

In the San Juan Mountains 25 miles north of Durango, with 1,650 acres, about 2,000 ft of vertical and 260 inches of snow a year. The trail mix leans advanced (43%), there are several terrain parks and an on-mountain urgent care clinic. Founded in 1965, it went by Durango Mountain Resort from 2000 to 2015.

A family-owned resort beside Pyhä-Luosto National Park in Finnish Lapland, about 1.5 hours from Rovaniemi, with easy-to-reach freeride terrain, uncrowded slopes, night skiing and a quiet Lapland feel, plus northern lights, ice climbing and reindeer.

Billed as the world's most northerly ski resort, about 200 km north of the Arctic Circle on the Norwegian border, with a season from February to June and lifts running under the midnight sun from late May. about.text: A family-friendly, alpine-urban pair of areas around Brixen in the Eisacktal: the Plose, whose 9 km Trametsch is one of South Tyrol's longest runs, and Gitschberg Jochtal, with the Gimmy snowparks for kids and the 6 km Brimi sledge run.
York County's night-skiing hill: 600 feet of vertical, 22 trails lit on 95% of the terrain seven nights a week, four terrain parks and snow tubing. Easy from Harrisburg and Baltimore.

Finland's most popular ski resort, in Kuusamo near the Arctic Circle, with a season that usually runs from October into May, 23 lifts, night skiing and a steep-leaning mix of runs for a Finnish fell, plus northern lights. Kuusamo airport is about 20 km away.

access.notes: 5 consecutive days. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: The largest resort in Hokkaido, with three mountains (West, East and Isola), 37 runs and 19 lifts including four gondolas, and repeated "Japan's Best Ski Resort" awards. The Westin and other hotels sleep up to 4,000, and there's an amusement park with eight roller coasters for summer.

A car-free village at 1,800 m ringed by 13 peaks over 4,000 m, the most in the Alps. The Metro Alpin, the world's highest underground funicular, climbs to Mittelallalin and its revolving restaurant at 3,500 m, and the glaciers keep snow sports going all year. 150 km of runs, more than half of them easy.

access.notes: Reservations are encouraged here but not required.
Reservations are encouraged here but not required.

about.text: Revived in 2020 after five dark winters, near Rangeley in the western Maine mountains. The upper mountain's Kennebago Steeps and big glades like Casablanca draw experts; the lower mountain is gentle and wide. Lift-top views over lakes and mountains, trails named for fishing flies and a local, independent spirit.

access.notes: Two tickets for one voucher, same day only. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: A small, quiet fell resort in eastern Lapland near the Russian border, with about 10 km of pistes on 15 slopes, floodlit night skiing, an FIS slalom slope used by Finland's national team, a freestyle area and about 160 km of cross-country trails, plus reindeer, huskies and northern lights. Helly Hansen's offer here is two tickets for one voucher.

about.text: San Martino di Castrozza and the Rolle Pass in southern Trentino, around the Pala group, with lifts reaching high above the village, enchanting views of the Pale di San Martino, snowparks and the well-known Tognola slopes.

The former Suicide Six, run by the Woodstock Inn, where America's first ski tow reportedly turned in 1934. It's small, about 650 feet of vertical with full snowmaking and a terrain park, and pairs best with a weekend in the village of Woodstock. Low-key and historic rather than big.
A Fraser Valley mountain near Agassiz, a short drive from Vancouver's suburbs, with 36 trails, powder-filled bowls, parks and night skiing.

Schladming's ski mountains in Styria, led by the Planai, which has held World Cup races since 1973, a floodlit Nightrace since 1997, and the World Championships in 1982 and 2013. Planai's red and black runs suit good skiers, with blues for beginners; Hochwurzen and Reiteralm are close by.

access.notes: 5 days total across Skicircus Saalbach Hinterglemm Leogang Fieberbrunn, Schmittenhöhe (Zell am See) and Kitzsteinhorn (Kaprun) (Saalbach, Zell am See and Kaprun). Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: The Schmittenhöhe rises straight out of the lakeside town of Zell am See to about 2,000 m, with views over the lake and the Hohe Tauern. It's a lower-altitude mountain known for its steep Trassabfahrt and the old Tannwald racing piste, and one pass covers it together with the Kitzsteinhorn glacier above Kaprun.

The ski hill at Shanty Creek Resort in Bellaire, with 42 runs, a surprising share of advanced terrain, parks, night skiing, tubing and cross-country trails. Budget-friendly with resort lodging on site.
North Idaho's big mountain above Lake Pend Oreille, with 2,900 acres, more than 300 inches of snow and a small village at the top of the access road. Laid-back, small-town feel near Sandpoint.

about.text: Lake Placid's community Nordic center, run by High Peaks Cyclery: about 15 km on 10 trails, most of them beginner, with night skiing, dog-friendly trails and a restaurant and bar.

Three villages on a plateau 500 m above Tyrol's upper Inn valley, sharing 190 km of pistes and 70 lifts. Serfaus banned cars in the 1970s and moves guests on the Dorfbahn, a free four-stop underground railway opened in 1985 and one of the smallest in the world.

A string of villages along the valley from Briançon to Le Monêtier-les-Bains, sharing 250 km of slopes from 1,200 to 2,800 m. The tree line sits at 2,150 m, so about 700 m of vertical runs through forest, and the valley gets around 300 sunny days a year. It hosts freestyle skiing at the 2030 Winter Olympics.

Giovanni Agnelli's purpose-built resort of the 1930s on a 2,035 m pass, at the heart of the Via Lattea: up to 400 km of runs shared with Sauze d'Oulx, Claviere, Montgenèvre and others. It hosted all the men's alpine events at the 2006 Olympics, still holds World Cup races and floodlights a run for night skiing.
Western Pennsylvania's big resort in the Laurel Highlands: 40 trails, seven terrain parks, night skiing and an on-site hotel. Events like Brewski Fest and the spring pond skim keep it lively.
A co-op-run mountain in the Coast Mountains 35 km west of Terrace, with about 480 inches of snow, natural glades and 1,600 feet of vertical. Deep, quiet and community-owned.

resorts.name: Shawnee Mountain Ski Area
resorts.learnToTurn: Learn to Turn partner in 25/26: Indy's beginner pass (lift ticket for beginner terrain, a lesson and rentals, 3 days for $189). The 26/27 list isn't out yet.

about.text: A family-run Poconos mountain in East Stroudsburg with 23 trails, heavy snowmaking, careful grooming, parks and day-and-night skiing. Its kids' programs and tubing park make it a family favorite.

Arguably Japan's largest ski resort: 18 interconnected areas and about 50 lifts in Joshinetsu Kogen National Park, reaching about 2,300 m at Yokoteyama, one of the highest ski areas in Japan, with a season from November into early May. It hosted 1998 Olympic technical races, and many hotels have their own hot-spring baths. Ikon's days count across all 18 areas.

A small, locally loved resort in the Hachimantai area of Iwate, in a sheltered east-facing bowl known for deep, very light powder. The draw is tree skiing and backcountry off three lifts, and the ticket also covers the beginner-friendly Panorama area, a 10-minute shuttle away, which has night skiing.
Montana's oldest ski area, near Neihart, with 640 acres, 1,400 feet of vertical, parks and night skiing. Powder-focused and family-friendly.
A mid-sized, family-geared resort south of Lake Tahoe near Twin Bridges, with heavy snowfall and six terrain parks.
Kellogg's mountain, 30 minutes east of Coeur d'Alene, reached by what it calls America's longest gondola. 1,600 acres plus the Silver Rapids indoor waterpark make it a year-round family base.
A colorful, true ski-in/ski-out village at 1,609 metres above Vernon, with 133 marked runs, 760 metres of vertical, dry Okanagan snow and a huge Nordic network shared with Sovereign Lake.

access.notes: Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: Vorarlberg's biggest area, stretching 17 km along the Montafon valley from Schruns to Gaschurn: 141 km of pistes and 35 lifts, with more than half the runs above 2,000 m, 28 km of freeride routes and a large terrain park that hosts a snowboard-cross World Cup each December.
A member-owned, volunteer-run club near Syracuse since 1959: seven trails, surface lifts and lights for night skiing. Friday-night potlucks and a cardboard sled race set the tone.
A young community ski area in Hatcher Pass near Palmer, with 12 trails, terrain parks and night skiing. Playful and local.

Owned and run by the Mescalero Apache Tribe since 1963, on Sierra Blanca near Ruidoso, with 750 acres from a 9,600 ft base to 11,500 ft. Its gondola is the only one serving ski runs in New Mexico, and Sierra Blanca Trail runs about 2.5 miles. About 15 feet of snow a year, two terrain parks and zip lines.

access.notes: Only with a stay at a participating Arlberg lodging property, booked direct (minimum nights vary). 3 consecutive days. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: St. Anton, St. Christoph, Stuben, Lech, Zürs, Warth and Schröcken make up Austria's largest linked ski area, with more than 300 km of groomed pistes, 85 lifts and over 200 km of ungroomed ski routes for freeriders. The Arlberg is where one of the first ski schools opened in 1921, and the 22 km White Ring tour links five descents above Lech and Zürs. St. Anton's après scene is one of the liveliest in the Alps.

about.text: A family hill at Masthope Mountain near Lackawaxen in the northern Poconos, with 18 trails, a terrain park, snow tubing and night skiing. Private beginner lessons are a specialty, and it's a Learn to Turn partner.

about.text: A family-friendly, affordable mountain in Washington's Blue Mountains near Dayton, with a high 4,545-foot base, about 300 inches of snow and 450 acres. A Learn to Turn partner.

access.notes: Bonus mountain. Ikon lists blackout dates for some bonus mountains without naming them, so they are shown here.

about.text: A Berkshires family hill in Great Barrington with 1,000 feet of vertical, 22 trails, two terrain parks, a tubing area and a PSIA ski school. Relaxed and easy, close to the restaurants of Great Barrington.
North America's northernmost lift-served ski area, near Fairbanks, with 58 trails over 550 acres, parks and a good chance of skiing under the northern lights.
A beginner-friendly hill 25 minutes from Montreal with 18 trails, parks, night skiing under the lights and music nights. Great for first days and family outings.

The southernmost major ski area in the Rockies, 16 miles above Santa Fe in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, with a base at 10,350 ft and a 12,075 ft summit. 660 acres and 88 trails, 40% of them advanced, and three terrain parks. New Mexico's first rope tow ran here in 1936.
A relaxed family hill near Pennsylvania's Grand Canyon in Morris, with 13 slopes, a big-feature terrain park, tubing and night skiing. It has a small inn with Jacuzzi rooms and group lodging on site.

A small Laurentian hill in Val-David's snow belt, open since 1963 and unchanged in character, with 52 short trails, a steeper mix than you'd expect and a family-first policy. No night skiing or parks.

access.notes: Indy's discounted third day isn't offered here.

about.text: One of Austria's biggest linked areas, around Söll, Ellmau, Scheffau and the Brixental, with 82 lifts, over 270 km of runs and about 80 family-run huts, under an hour from Salzburg, Innsbruck and Munich. Mostly wide, easy terrain with 22 ski schools, plus night skiing and parks. Indy's discounted third day isn't offered here.

access.notes: 5 days total across Skicircus Saalbach Hinterglemm Leogang Fieberbrunn, Schmittenhöhe (Zell am See) and Kitzsteinhorn (Kaprun) (Saalbach, Zell am See and Kaprun). Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: One of Austria's biggest linked areas: about 270 km of pistes connecting Saalbach, Hinterglemm, Leogang and Fieberbrunn on modern heated six- and eight-seat chairs. The sunny side of the valley is for cruising and the shady north-facing side holds snow later in the season, with off-piste powder close to the pistes. It hosted the 1991 and 2025 Alpine World Championships, and Saalbach's après is famously loud.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: The Gastein valley's ski areas (Schlossalm, Stubnerkogel, Graukogel and Sportgastein) with over 200 km of slopes in the Ski amadé network, above the thermal spa towns of Bad Gastein and Bad Hofgastein, which hosted the 1958 World Championships and still host snowboard World Cups.

about.text: A family-run inn and Nordic center in Huntington with about 32 km of classic and skate trails and separate snowshoe routes. A lit 3 km loop is open for night skiing three evenings a week. Lessons cover every level, with rentals for kids as young as three.

about.text: Labrador City's mountain with 960 feet of vertical, steep walls and open faces, about 177 inches of snow a year, parks and night skiing. A new carpet lift helps beginners; a Learn to Turn partner.

about.text: Three connected peaks with a reputation as one of the most family-focused resorts in the country and a highly ranked ski school. Morse Mountain is the gentle learning hill by the village; Sterling and Madonna hold the steeper terrain, including the Black Hole, billed as Vermont's only triple black. Expect a slopeside village and kids' programs rather than a nightlife scene.
Kansas City's ski area in Weston, Missouri, with short runs, terrain parks, night skiing and the Tornado Alley tubing park. Owned by Vail Resorts.
Jackson Hole's original ski area, right above the town of Jackson, with 1,560 feet of vertical, night skiing and an affordable, local feel.

On the Tug Hill Plateau, one of the snowiest places in the East: about 230 inches of lake-effect snow a year. Only 500 feet of vertical, but mostly advanced terrain, plus parks and night skiing. Deep snow and a long history.
Southern California's longest continuously operating ski resort, in Running Springs, with 29 trails over 240 acres, a good share of harder runs and night skiing.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: Host of the 2002 Olympic downhill and speed events, and slated to host again in 2034: 3,000 acres and 104 runs above Ogden, with grand, comfortable day lodges and usually manageable crowds.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: Little Cottonwood Canyon's big, steep mountain, with more than 500 inches of snow a year, a tram to Hidden Peak, a tunnel to Mineral Basin and one of the longest seasons in the West. The Cliff Lodge sits at the base.

Western Upper Peninsula big-snow country near Wakefield, formed from two neighboring ski areas: 53 main trails, 19 sidecountry runs, two terrain parks and ten lifts. Some of the Midwest's deepest natural snow.

The South's biggest resort, built upside down with its village on top of the mountain and 1,500-foot runs like Cupp Run dropping below. Around 1,400 condo and hotel units sit in the village, and 100% snowmaking keeps it reliable.
A park-focused hill in Andalusia, Illinois, with a 28-acre terrain park of 40-plus features, 11 tubing lanes and night skiing. A community staple since 1981.

access.notes: Bonus mountain. Ikon lists blackout dates for some bonus mountains without naming them, so they are shown here.

about.text: A small Wyoming area about 32 miles from Laramie, with 27 trails on 250 acres and 865 feet of vertical. A relaxed local outing.

about.text: Idaho's best-kept secret, 12 miles north of Fairfield, with terrain from beginner to advanced, jump trails and snowcat skiing across about 2,000 acres of backcountry. A Learn to Turn partner.
A quieter Big Cottonwood Canyon resort with bowl skiing in Honeycomb Canyon, a balanced trail mix, a Nordic center and Creekside lodging. A good family alternative to its busier neighbors.

The flagship of Les Sommets in the Laurentians, with 41 trails and nine lifts, 28 of the trails lit for night skiing. Its snow school is billed as the best in Quebec, and about $30 million is going into 2026-27, including a new six-person chairlift and La Place du Sommet.

about.text: One of Canada's top Nordic areas, under 30 minutes from Vernon: 105 km of daily-groomed trails shared with SilverStar, a high sub-alpine setting, dry snow and night skiing.

access.notes: 5 days total across the 5 Zillertal areas. Epic says the mobile pass can't be used for lift access here; bring the physical pass card.

about.text: A certified family ski mountain above Fügen at the mouth of the Zillertal, reached by a barrier-free gondola to about 2,000 m, with a kids' adventure playground and guest kindergarten at the top, ski schools, tobogganing and a bistro and restaurant at the base.
