about.text: Duluth's mountain with Lake Superior views, 700 feet of vertical and 22 trails, plus more than 30 km of Nordic trails across two linked centers. Night skiing on both. Family-friendly and a Learn to Turn partner.

A lesson-first family hill in Schwenksville, outside Philadelphia, with more than 100 instructors a season, two terrain parks, night skiing and a full-size outdoor skating rink. Après is the Powder Pig Pub.
A family resort at the foot of the Kitzbüheler Horn with groomed, mostly easy and intermediate runs from three access points, kids' practice areas and family-run huts.

Famous for its dry champagne powder and tree skiing like the Shadows glades, near the Western town of Steamboat Springs. The Sunshine Peak expansion and Wild Blue Gondola have made it bigger than ever.

about.text: Steamboat's Nordic center since 1980, right below the gondola at the base of the ski resort, with about 20 km of groomed trails.

A family ski area where Tyrol, Salzburg and Bavaria meet, reached from Waidring in Austria or Reit im Winkl in Germany, with 42 km of easy and intermediate slopes, a dinosaur-themed fun line, a three-section snowpark and rustic huts.
A Cascades mountain on US 2 with numerous bowls, glades and faces and plenty of lit terrain for night skiing. A popular day trip from the Seattle area.

access.notes: 7 days total across Fernie Alpine Resort, Kicking Horse, Kimberley Alpine Resort, Nakiska, Mont-Sainte-Anne and Stoneham (Resorts of the Canadian Rockies).

about.text: North of Quebec City, with 42 trails across four mountains, three terrain parks and Canada's biggest night-skiing network. It has hosted snowboard and alpine World Cups.

access.notes: Holiday blockouts apply.

about.text: Classic Vermont skiing on Mount Mansfield, the state's highest peak, linked by gondola to Spruce Peak and its village. The mix leans intermediate to advanced, and the 4.3-mile Toll Road gives newer skiers a top-to-bottom cruise. The town of Stowe is one of the East's best spots for après and dining, with an upscale feel and prices to match.

access.notes: New for 26/27.

about.text: A Norwegian freeride favourite above the Storfjord near the UNESCO-listed Geirangerfjord, where you ski steep, snowy terrain with the fjord's deep blue water below. Heavy snow, night skiing and a terrain park. New to Indy for 26/27.

Southern Vermont's polished village resort, with a summit gondola, about 95% snowmaking and lots of groomed cruising. Around 40% of trails are easier and the learning area was rebuilt in 2023. Stratton was the first ski area to allow snowboarding, and its après tradition dates to the Austrian instructors of the 1960s.

Austria's largest glacier ski area, at the head of the Stubai valley, with snow guaranteed from October to June on 41 km of pistes between 1,750 and 3,210 m. More than half the runs are easy; there's the 10 km Wilde Grube valley run, freeride terrain and the Stubai Zoo snowpark.

access.notes: Free day of skiing for one voucher. Uses one voucher; it must be used on that visit. Helly Hansen's list as of 12 Oct 2026; partners can change.

about.text: The main resort of Sälen in Dalarna near the Norwegian border, with the biggest vertical in the area, 23 lifts and a mostly easy mix that still has some steeper runs, plus terrain parks.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: A historic, privately owned Tahoe resort with about 500 inches of snow a year, where a gondola from the parking lot carries skiers to the village. Mt. Disney is named for early investor Walt Disney, and nearly 40% of trails are advanced.

Two mountains joined by one of the longest chairlifts anywhere: Lincoln Peak with its village, and the more old-school Mt. Ellen. Experts come for Castlerock's narrow, natural-snow trails and the woods of Slide Brook Basin; intermediates get plenty of cruisers. The Mad River Valley around it has a laid-back, local feel.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: Remote, big and proudly Maine: the only lift-served skiing above treeline in the Northeast, the Brackett Basin glades and dozens of double blacks. A car-free base village puts lodging steps from the lifts, and Bullwinkle's on the mountain and the Widowmaker Lounge at the base carry the après. Summit views reach the White Mountains.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: Canada's second-largest ski area, near Kamloops: 144 trails, a ski-in/ski-out village, more than 2,000 hours of sunshine a year and extensive Nordic trails. Family-friendly and lively.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: America's first destination ski resort, where the world's first chairlifts turned in 1936. Bald Mountain's long, steady fall line suits intermediates and experts; Dollar Mountain is for beginners. Immaculate grooming, short lift lines and a classy, relaxed feel.
A family hill since 1961, 30 minutes from Milwaukee, with 11 trails, parks, night skiing and what it calls the world's largest tubing hill. Traditional, local and affordable.

Robert Redford's resort on the slopes of Mount Timpanogos, 13 miles from Provo, which he bought in 1968 and named after his Sundance Kid role; the Sundance Film Festival grew out of it. About 2,150 ft of vertical up to Bearclaw Cabin, with 40% of the trails rated advanced. Redford sold it in 2020.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: One of New England's biggest resorts: eight connected peaks, about 870 acres and 2,340 feet of vertical, with 95% snowmaking that keeps it open early and late. A third of the trails are beginner, the parks are well regarded and there are two slopeside hotels plus the town of Bethel nearby. Spring traditions include the Bust 'N' Burn mogul contest.

about.text: Sölden in the Ötztal reaches from about 1,350 m to 3,250 m across the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers, with 146 km of pistes and a long season. It opens the World Cup each October with giant slalom races on the Rettenbach glacier, and the village has one of Austria's biggest après scenes.
A large resort in Gujo, Gifu, with a 2.5 km gondola from base to summit, linked at the top with Dynaland for 32 courses on one ticket and a season from early December to late April.

about.text: An upscale, all-season ski, golf and lake resort near Donnelly, 90 miles from Boise, with 2,800 feet of vertical and 1,385 mostly intermediate acres.

access.notes: 2 free days here, then 50% off any additional day. No blackouts. Some destinations need advance reservations.

about.text: A steep, high New Mexico mountain with the Kachina lift reaching 12,481 feet and a small alpine village in the Carson National Forest. Known for its challenging terrain and its well-loved ski school.

Above Lake Tazawa, Japan's deepest lake, in Akita, where the west-facing slopes catch heavy Sea of Japan storms. High-speed lifts, groomers, side- and backcountry, and an annual FIS Freestyle World Cup mogul event.

about.text: A West Kelowna Nordic center with 50 km of ski trails, 50 km of snowshoe trails, night skiing and a reputation for top grooming.

A free gondola links the historic town of Telluride with Mountain Village, and the views of the San Juans are some of the best in skiing. About 41% of runs are advanced or expert, with plenty of long cruisers too.

about.text: A revived independent hill in Plymouth with about 1,500 feet of vertical, narrow winding trails and natural glades. The community brought it back after years of closures, and the Hornet double is New Hampshire's oldest operating chairlift. Friendly staff and a renovated lodge with live music round it out.
The Black Hills' big mountain near Lead and Deadwood: a 7,100-foot summit, 1,100 feet of vertical, 30 mostly intermediate and advanced trails, high-speed quads and about 150 inches of snow.

A Nagano resort with a ski-in/ski-out hotel and easy access from Tokyo, powder runs on slopes up to 46 degrees, a solid terrain park, good kids' facilities and an 800 m sledding course, the longest in eastern Japan.
Now The Highlands at Harbor Springs, near Petoskey: one of northern Michigan's biggest ski areas, spread across several peaks with lodging and dining at the base.

Seattle's ski area, 52 miles east on I-90, with four base areas from beginner slopes to Alpental's steeps, night skiing and Nordic trails at Summit East.

about.text: A European-style village in the Snowy Mountains with the steepest overall terrain on mainland Australia, lifts up to 2,037 m and Australia's longest single run, the Crackenback Supertrail. Merritts Gondola opened in 2020, and the village has lodges, shops and nightlife.
A small hill in the river breaks near Fort Ransom with 10 easy and intermediate trails and an updated lodge with hot food, a full bar and a fireplace.

Jean-Claude Killy's home mountains, also called Espace Killy: Tignes and Val d'Isère share 300 km of pistes, 90 lifts and two glaciers in the Tarentaise valley. Nearly half the runs are red or black, and there are two terrain parks and 44 km of cross-country trails.

On Mount Hood's south face, 60 miles from Portland, with the only lift-served skiing in the U.S. all twelve months, on the Palmer Glacier above 7,000 ft. 1,685 acres and 4,540 ft of vertical, about 45 ft of snow a year. The lodge, built by the WPA in 1936-38, is a National Historic Landmark.

about.text: Three connected peaks near Malone in New York's far north, with 53 runs, 1,200 feet of vertical and about 150 inches of snow. Slopeside chalets, a tubing hill, parks and night skiing, with a strong family reputation.
A quiet Nagano area with uncrowded weekdays, two peaks, 19 runs including wooded runs and easy sidecountry, and an old-fashioned base. The village is famous for soba noodles and its ninja history.
A laid-back hot-spring village resort in northern Nagano with dependable natural snow, uncrowded slopes, an even beginner-intermediate mix, night skiing and a terrain park.

about.text: America's first commercial cross-country ski center, founded in 1968 by the von Trapp family above Stowe. It has 60-plus km of groomed trails plus backcountry, with a cabin mid-trail serving soup and hot chocolate. Back at the lodge there's a brewery and Bierhall with Austrian flair.

about.text: A Gaylord resort with 25 short trails, parks, night skiing, tubing and a first-timer program, plus a handful of cross-country trails. Family-friendly with lodging on site.

Eastern Canada's marquee resort in the Laurentians: about 2,100 feet of vertical across four sides and a car-free village at the base with hotels, shops and restaurants. Magic carpets for newcomers, steeper terrain on the north side, and real cold on January mornings.
A classic mom-and-pop hill in Dresser, about 50 minutes from the Twin Cities, with 30 trails, a strong park reputation, night skiing and a mid-century chalet with the Skolhaugen Lounge.

Norway's largest ski resort: 69 slopes and 41 lifts on Trysilfjellet, spread out in three directions, from long, wide carving runs in Høgegga to gentle runs for families. Large children's areas, terrain parks, ski-in/ski-out lodging and heated chairlifts.
A snow-reliable village area in Graubünden's Schanfigg valley above Chur, with 32 km of natural-snow slopes, four lifts, good freeride terrain and far fewer people than the big resorts.

about.text: A big, snowy resort at the north end of the valley with about 900 m of vertical, a 1,200 m-wide gentle area for beginners and families, a kids' area, an onsen and a powder zone, Tsuga-Pow, for stronger skiers. Half the terrain is rated beginner.

about.text: A wilderness ranch near Jackson with 20 km of loops designed by Olympic athletes across rolling fields, with Grand Teton views.
Happy Valley's town mountain, minutes from Penn State: eight trails, terrain parks and night skiing. A popular place in central Pennsylvania to learn.
A family-friendly hill in Mount Horeb, 18 miles west of Madison, with 24 runs, a solid share of advanced terrain, parks and night skiing.

about.text: Funäsfjällen's flagship hill, named Sweden's Best Ski Resort at the 2025 World Ski Awards, with 57 runs above and below the treeline across the valley, 4-5 m of natural snow a winter, snowparks, evening skiing, three kids' areas and off-piste touring at Hamra Syd. Funäsfjällen adds about 300 km of cross-country tracks, and two new lifts open for 26/27.

about.text: One of America's biggest single mountains at over 5,000 acres: miles of front-side groomers, the wide-open Back Bowls and the remote feel of Blue Sky Basin. Bavarian-style, car-free Vail Village is the après hub.

access.notes: 7 days total across the 12 Dolomiti Superski areas. Valid 15 Nov 2026 to 15 Apr 2027.

about.text: Ortisei, Santa Cristina and Selva in South Tyrol, on the Sella Ronda circuit around the Sella massif, with access to more than 500 km of linked skiing. The Saslong, one of the five classic men's downhills with its famous Camel Humps, has been raced here almost every year since 1969.

A small hill in Sainte-Irène, about four hours from Quebec City, with one of eastern Canada's biggest snowfalls (around 228 inches) and an expert ridge of 14 ungroomed glades and chutes. Lively events, including an April pond crossing.

about.text: Trentino's Ladin valley (Canazei, Campitello, Pozza, Vigo and Moena) with six ski areas and a gateway to the Sella Ronda, plus Carezza under the Rosengarten beside Lake Carezza with its snowpark and huts. Known for views of the Sassolungo and the pink alpenglow on the Catinaccio and Latemar. Aloch at Pozza hosts European Cup slaloms.

about.text: A purpose-built resort in the Andes about 46 km east of Santiago, modelled partly on France's Les Arcs, with a base at about 3,000 m, around 900 hectares of terrain, about 7 m of snow a year, a terrain park and Chile's first mountain gondola. The season traditionally runs June to October.

about.text: Verbier anchors the western end of the 4 Vallées, a linked area with Nendaz, Veysonnaz, La Tzoumaz and Thyon that climbs to 3,330 m on Mont Fort. It's known worldwide for off-piste: the Tortin and Gentianes mogul fields, Mont Gelé with no marked runs, and the Bec des Rosses face that hosts the Freeride World Tour final. Beginners get a dedicated snow garden, and the village draws a famously glamorous crowd.

A volunteer-run community ski area in Franklin, operated by the Franklin Outing Club in a 680-acre conservation forest. It's a small local hill with Thursday-evening skiing, sledding and year-round trails. Check its site for the current season's status before you go.

The big hill in central Massachusetts, in Princeton near Worcester, with 1,006 ft of vertical, 27 trails, snowmaking on all of them and night skiing on most. The Civilian Conservation Corps cut its first trails in the 1930s, and the 10th Mountain Division trained here in World War II.

In Gujo, Gifu, about 3 km from the Takasu interchange, with ski-in/ski-out lodging, an even spread of runs for beginners through advanced skiers, night skiing and a terrain park. It links to WhitePIA Takasu.

about.text: A planned resort village in the White Mountains with about 1,500 feet of vertical, 97% snowmaking and a strong freestyle streak: six terrain parks, including the Boneyard, reportedly New Hampshire's first. The valley adds 40-plus miles of Nordic trails, skating and indoor activities, so it works for mixed groups. It has night skiing on select nights.

An upstate favorite at the foot of the Adirondacks off I-87, with 1,000 feet of vertical, 35 trails, an expanded learning area, parks, tubing and night skiing. The bar and eatery runs live music and theme nights.

A community-run, nonprofit hill in Enfield just off I-89, with about 700 feet of vertical, terrain parks and night skiing. It's a local, scrappy favorite for park riders and after-work laps around the Upper Valley.

A Gujo, Gifu, resort with views of the Hakusan range, a balanced mix of runs and a terrain park. It connects with neighbouring Washigatake.
Three peaks in Wisconsin's Penokee Mountains with 48 runs and about 200 inches of snow a year. Authentic Northwoods ski country with a laid-back, local welcome.

about.text: The biggest vertical in the East, over 3,100 feet from one lift, plus the Slides' double-black off-piste for the brave. Site of the 1980 Olympic alpine events, near Lake Placid's restaurants and lodging. Expect wind and ice up top; dress for it.

Big Mountain above the town of Whitefish in northwest Montana, just west of Glacier National Park, with 3,020 skiable acres, 2,353 ft of vertical and about 300 inches of snow a year. The Hellroaring basin holds cliffs, steep chutes and tight trees, and Hell Fire runs 2.5 miles. Open since 1947; Olympic champion Tommy Moe learned to race here.

about.text: Whitehorse's Nordic center on Mount McIntyre, near downtown, with 93 km of classic and skate trails, three warming huts, a sauna and the chance to ski under the northern lights.

The closest bigger mountain to DC and Baltimore, about 90 miles out, with 935 feet of vertical and night skiing on nearly every trail. Beginner, intermediate and expert zones are laid out separately. Busy on weekends, quiet midweek.

A powder bowl in the Selkirks just outside Nelson, BC, with about 12 m (472 in) of dry snow a year and a 62% advanced trail mix known for tree skiing and steeps. About 1,320 acres since the Glory expansion and four chairs, plus Nordic trails and an award-winning cafeteria. Opened in 1976.

Across Pinkham Notch from Mount Washington, with some of the best mountain views in New England and the most vertical off a single lift in the region. Polecat is the longest trail in New Hampshire, a gentle 2.75-mile cruise from the summit. There's no lodging at the base and no terrain park; it's about the skiing and the scenery.

The self-styled Matterhorn of the Midwest, 55 miles north of Chicago: wide-open trails, all lit for night skiing, plus tubing and kids' programs. Owned by Vail Resorts.

Denver's own big mountain, reachable on the Winter Park Express ski train. Mary Jane's moguls and trees are the challenge, Parsenn Bowl adds open terrain above treeline, and the Winter Park side has plenty of cruisers.

A nonprofit mountain in Vernon, New Jersey, built for young skiers and riders, with affordable lessons, camps, racing, terrain parks and night skiing. It describes itself as the country's only youth-focused resort, so check its rules for adults before you go.
A Blue Ridge resort near Charlottesville with about 1,000 feet of vertical and a steeper mix than most of the South, nearly half advanced. Night skiing, parks and condos and homes on the mountain.
Five minutes off I-77 in southern West Virginia, with 27 slopes, full snowmaking, night skiing, parks and the state's biggest tubing park. It bills itself as the Southeast's top place to learn.

Maryland's only ski resort, above Deep Creek Lake, with 33 trails, 700 feet of vertical, parks and night skiing. Ski-in/ski-out rooms at the Lodge at Wisp and a mountain coaster make it an easy family weekend.

On Wolf Creek Pass between Pagosa Springs and South Fork, with more snow than any other Colorado resort: about 430 inches a year, and a state-record 807 inches in 1978-79. 1,600 acres and 77 trails from a 10,300 ft base; the longest run, Navajo Trail, is 2 miles.

Easy loops on the golf course suit beginners, with pulk sleds for small kids. Then you're steps from one of Vermont's prettiest villages.

about.text: Lapland's second-biggest resort, on Finland's highest lift-served fell, with 61 slopes and 29 lifts between the villages of Äkäslompolo and Ylläsjärvi, about 330 km of cross-country trails and a gondola with a sauna cabin. Helly Hansen's free day covers the Äkäslompolo side.

About an hour from Beijing by high-speed rail, a competition venue with a halfpipe, slopestyle course and parallel giant slalom track. It hosted freestyle and snowboard events at the 2022 Winter Olympics, where Ayumu Hirano landed his triple cork. 45 trails, with hotels by the gondola.
One of the snowiest spots in the Yuzawa area of Niigata (Indy lists an average over 500 inches), with beginner slopes for first-timers plus ungroomed areas and tree runs for experienced riders.

A historic hot-spring town in Yamagata whose upper slopes are famous for "snow monsters", firs encased in rime by Siberian winds. The 9 km Snow Monster Course winds through them. About 880 m of vertical across 25 trails, and sulphurous onsen in the village.

about.text: The car-free Swiss village under the Matterhorn, with four areas (Sunnegga, Gornergrat, Schwarzsee and the Klein Matterhorn, whose glacier lifts reach 3,883 m) and a link over the Plateau Rosa glacier to Cervinia in Italy. One of the few places to ski in summer, on the Theodul glacier, though August 2026 heat paused it.

about.text: The largest linked ski area in the Zillertal, connecting Zell am Ziller, Gerlos, Königsleiten and Hochkrimml across the Tyrol-Salzburg border: about 150 km of pistes and some 50 lifts up to about 2,500 m, with a reputation for reliable snow.

Sweden's World Championship resort, on the Åreskutan in Jämtland, with about 100 km of runs, 46 lifts including a funicular and a gondola, and three terrain parks. It hosted the Alpine World Championships in 1954, 2007 and 2019; the summit café, open since 1892, is the highest in Sweden.
